summary: Extended the Spanish Treaty Claims Commission's powers to examine and settle U.S. citizens' claims against Spain until March 2, 1907.
Enlarged the Diamond Mountain Forest Reserve, first proclaimed July 14, 1905, by adding partly timbered lands in California and reserving them from settlement.
Set the ceremony for presenting the Medal of Honor to Navy enlisted men and officers, with recipients ordered to Washington, when practicable, to receive it from the President or his representative.
Proclaimed Thursday, November 29, 1906, a day of national thanksgiving and prayer for the year's blessings.

Directed that Cuba's temporary government be run in Havana by the Provisional Governor under the Secretary of War, with related business in the United States handled by the War Department's Bureau of Insular Affairs.
Set aside the abandoned part of the New Fort Lyon Military Reservation in Bent County, Colorado, and its buildings for the Navy Department to use as a sanitarium.
Reserved a tract on the glacial flats of Valdez Glacier, north of the town of Valdez, Alaska, as a target range for the troops of Fort Liscum.
Allowed Paul A. Hines, a clerk in the office of the Secretary of Agriculture, to be promoted without a civil-service examination.
Created the Sierra Madre Forest Reserve in Wyoming, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.
Established the Gallinas Forest Reserve in New Mexico Territory, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.
Enlarged the Chiricahua Forest Reserve, first proclaimed July 30, 1902, by adding partly timbered lands in Arizona Territory and reserving them from settlement.
Set apart the Magdalena Forest Reserve in New Mexico Territory, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.
Created the San Mateo Forest Reserve in New Mexico Territory, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.
Established the Peloncillo Forest Reserve in New Mexico Territory, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.
Set apart the Lemhi Forest Reserve in Idaho, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.
Created the Raft River Forest Reserve, spanning Idaho and Utah, and reserved the described timbered public lands from settlement.
Established the Snowy Mountains Forest Reserve in Montana, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.
Set apart the Ekalaka Forest Reserve in Montana, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.
Created the Big Hole Forest Reserve in Montana, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.
Enlarged the Kootenai Forest Reserve in Montana, proclaimed August 13, 1906, by adding partly timbered lands across the line in Idaho.
Established the Charleston Forest Reserve in Nevada, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.
Set apart the Independence Forest Reserve in Nevada, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.
Created the Baboquivari Forest Reserve in Arizona Territory, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.
Established the Salmon River Forest Reserve in Idaho, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.
Abolished the Marshall Land District in Minnesota, whose office was at St. Cloud, and moved its lands and business to the Duluth Land District.

Permitted Albert M. West of Massachusetts to be reinstated as a scientific assistant in the Department of Agriculture despite the one-year limit of civil-service Rule IX, citing his unusual, expert qualifications.
Set apart the Huachuca Forest Reserve in Arizona Territory, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.
Created the Coeur d'Alene Forest Reserve in Idaho, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.
Added partly timbered lands in Idaho to the Priest River Forest Reserve of Idaho and Washington, first proclaimed February 22, 1897.
Established the Manzano Forest Reserve in New Mexico Territory, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.
Set apart the Pryor Mountains Forest Reserve in Montana, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.
Created the Missoula Forest Reserve in Montana, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.
Redrew the Little Belt Forest Reserve in Montana, adding partly timbered lands and excluding others; the excluded lands returned to the public domain and opened to settlement.
Enlarged the Lolo Forest Reserve, first proclaimed September 20, 1906, by adding partly timbered lands in Montana and reserving them from settlement.
Enlarged the Sawtooth Forest Reserve, first proclaimed May 29, 1905, by adding partly timbered lands in Idaho and reserving them from settlement.
Enlarged the Jemez Forest Reserve, first proclaimed October 12, 1905, by adding partly timbered lands in New Mexico Territory and reserving them from settlement.
Established the Taos Forest Reserve in New Mexico Territory, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.
Created the Tumacacori Forest Reserve in Arizona Territory, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.
Struck deputy collectors of internal revenue from the civil-service list of positions excepted from examination, bringing them under the examination requirement.

Reorganized the Isthmian Canal Commission: set quarterly sessions on the Isthmus, a four-member quorum, and its duties for building the canal, abolished its Executive Committee, and created an organization of the Chairman and department heads.
Reserved part of Cape Hinchinbrook on Hinchinbrook Island, Alaska, for lighthouse purposes.
Raised Navy pay $5 a month for men in their second enlistment and $3 more for each later one, and added special-duty pay for petty officers and apprentices who instruct apprentice seamen.

Designated the Grand Canyon Forest Reserve lands north and west of the Colorado River in Arizona Territory as a game preserve and breeding ground, making hunting or trapping game there unlawful except under Agriculture Department rules.

Set rules letting Navy enlisted men in their first enlistment buy their discharge in peacetime after one year, with the price tied to outfit cost and months served, and relief for men supporting destitute relatives.
Let Theodore C. M. Schindler be appointed a special agent in the Bureau of Corporations without a civil-service examination.

Proclaimed El Morro National Monument in New Mexico Territory, protecting the rocks known as El Morro and Inscription Rock, judged "of the greatest historical value," and warning against injuring them or settling the land.
Proclaimed Montezuma Castle National Monument in Arizona Territory, reserving the prehistoric structure known as Montezuma's Castle and surrounding land for its protection.

Created Petrified Forest National Monument to protect the fossilized wood of the "Petrified Forest" in Gila and Apache counties, Arizona Territory, warning against excavating, injuring or destroying the deposits.
Allowed William W. Gillespie to be appointed deputy collector in the Customs Service at Stamford, Connecticut, without examination.
Reserved the island called Rock of Ages in Lake Superior, Michigan, for lighthouse purposes.
Permitted Alfred W. Brown, former appraiser of merchandise at the port of Boston, to be reinstated in the classified Customs Service there without meeting civil-service rules.
Amended the June 27, 1906, Consular Service regulation so student interpreters are treated like vice consuls, deputy consuls and consular agents for appointment and promotion.

Let three Civil War veterans serving as temporary watchmen in the Interior Department — Philip M. Earle, Isaac Pearson and George F. Miller — be appointed permanently without regard to civil-service rules.
Allowed Kate Jones of Tennessee to move from classified laborer in the Patent Office to clerk at the Knoxville pension agency without examination.
Turned about 300 acres of the Fort Davis Military Reservation in Presidio County, Texas, no longer useful for military purposes, over to the Secretary of the Interior.
Withdrew public lands in township 16 north, range 1 east, New Mexico, from sale and settlement and set them apart for the Indians of the Jemez Pueblo.
Amended the consular fee schedule so owners of sealskin garments entering the United States from Canada pay no fee for an affidavit of temporary stay.
Allowed William A. Woodruff, a hospital attendant at Ellis Island, to transfer to a Treasury Department clerical job in Washington without meeting civil-service rules.
Let W. B. Johnson, a Government Printing Office compositor, transfer without examination to clerk in the Interior Department's Land Service.
Allowed Joseph J. Harvey, a messenger at the Spanish Treaty Claims Commission, to be transferred or appointed to any other subclerical civil-service position.
Changed Henry G. Balkam's status from skilled laborer to clerk in the Bureau of the Census, citing his valuable service and a coming cut in the laborer force.
Revoked the Camp Hartshorne military reservation on Laguan Island, Samar, Philippines, returning the land to the Philippine government for the benefit of its inhabitants.
Standardized naval vessel names: each Navy ship is officially designated by its name preceded only by "United States Ship" or "U.S.S."
Allowed Elza Eugene Phelps to be appointed a customs inspector for confidential duty on merchandise moving over the Tehuantepec National Railway in Mexico, without meeting civil-service rules.
Permitted Marshall M. Pool to be promoted without examination to a clerical job in the Army purchasing commissary's office at Kansas City, Missouri.
Let David Robinson be reinstated as an immigrant inspector, citing his efficiency and familiarity with immigration matters.
Reserved land at Waimānalo, Oahu, Hawaii, for lighthouse purposes at the Makapuʻu Light Station.
Established the Caribou Forest Reserve in Idaho and Wyoming, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.
Duplicates Executive Order 548, which authorized the Governor of Tutuila to issue certificates of protection to qualifying merchant vessels.

Empowered the Governor of Tutuila to issue certificates of protection, giving U.S. flag protection to merchant vessels owned by American citizens or by Tutuila and Manua residents who swore allegiance to the United States.
Reserved the building in Sitka, Alaska, formerly the governor's residence, for use as a naval hospital.
Added about 32.5 acres in Burleigh County, North Dakota, to the Fort Lincoln Military Reservation, reserving the lots from sale for military purposes.
Amended the regulations for the Army and Navy General Hospital at Hot Springs, Arkansas.
Enlarged the Camp John Hay Military Reservation at Baguio, Benguet, on Luzon in the Philippines, to take in additional public lands.
Proclaimed an additional agreement with Portugal, concluded November 19, 1902, extending the two nations' 1899 commercial reciprocity agreement to Porto Rico.
Expanded the Cascade Range Forest Reserve in Oregon, first proclaimed September 28, 1893, adding more partly timbered lands and reserving them from settlement.
Excused federal employees who belong to the Grand Army of the Republic from duty at noon on January 26, 1907, to attend the funeral of Russell A. Alger.
Allowed Frank P. Nantz to be appointed deputy collector of internal revenue at San Juan, Porto Rico, without meeting civil-service rules.
Let James Campbell, assistant appraiser of merchandise at Baltimore, be appointed deputy surveyor of customs at that port without meeting civil-service rules.
Moved the Isthmian Canal Commission's February 1907 quarterly session from the Isthmus of Panama to Washington, D.C.
Created the Ouray Forest Reserve in Colorado, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.
Extended the Spanish Treaty Claims Commission's powers to examine and settle U.S. citizens' claims against Spain until September 2, 1907.

Set rules letting Marine Corps enlisted men in their first enlistment buy their discharge in peacetime after one year, at $120, $100 or $90 depending on service, with relief for men supporting destitute relatives.
Established the Monticello Forest Reserve in Utah, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.
Set apart the Stony Creek Forest Reserve in California, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.
Created the Glenwood Forest Reserve in Utah, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.
Established the Big Burros Forest Reserve in New Mexico Territory, reserving the described timbered public lands from settlement.
Allowed Norman Oswell Cully to be appointed messenger to the superintendent of the Naval Academy without a civil-service examination.
Permitted Elizabeth M. Leech to be appointed to a clerical position in the classified civil service without meeting civil-service rules.
Reserved the Viti Rocks, or islands, in Bellingham Bay, Washington, for lighthouse purposes.
Let Mrs. George H. Hildreth be appointed to a clerical position in the Bureau of Pensions without examination.
Enlarged the San Jacinto Forest Reserve, first proclaimed February 22, 1897, by adding partly timbered lands in California and reserving them from settlement.
Cut lands out of the Little Belt Forest Reserve in Montana and restored them to the public domain.
Allowed Mazie R. Fountaine, a former Smithsonian Institution clerk, to be reinstated as a Treasury Department clerk without meeting civil-service rules.
Broadened Mrs. George H. Hildreth's exemption so she may take any clerical position in the classified service without examination, revoking the February 13 order limited to the Bureau of Pensions.
